extracted.intended_audience: BOEM stakeholders, offshore renewable energy developers (lessees/grant holders), certified verification agents, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements related to BOEM's proposed revisions to 30 CFR part 585 for OCS renewable energy, and instructions for preparing and submitting public comments. Covers procedural rules for leasing/grants, plan submittal, financial assurance, CVA duties, auctions, safety systems, and how the public should format comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contact information with comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include your name, address, and telephone number or email address so BOEM can contact you with any questions regarding your submission. BOEM will not consider anonymous comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and confidentiality of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses will be posted on https://www.regulations.gov. Your entire comment will become publicly available after submission, including your name, address, phone number, email address, and any other personally identifiable information (PII) in your comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to protect the confidentiality of your comments, clearly mark the relevant sections and request that BOEM treat them as confidential. To withhold PII, identify information that would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of privacy and briefly describe possible harmful consequences (embarrassment, injury, other harm). Label privileged/confidential information as 'Contains Confidential Information' and consider submitting such information as a separate attachment. Information not labeled may be regarded as suitable for public release. BOEM cannot guarantee it will be able to withhold PII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection comments timing
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB is required to provide its comments concerning the information collection in this proposed rule 30-60 days after publication of this document in the Federal Register. Therefore, a comment to OMB is best assured of being fully considered if OMB receives it by March 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not affect the deadline for public comments to BOEM on the proposed rule. To review the information collection request submitted to OMB, use https://www.reginfo.gov and follow the provided steps to find OMB Control Number 1010-0176.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of comments BOEM seeks
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM seeks public comments on the changes in regulatory text and interpretation contained in this proposed rule and on several specific areas of inquiry for which it is not proposing regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will consider whether this proposed rule or any additional modifications would improve, clarify, or streamline its OCS renewable regulations. Based on comments received and its experience, BOEM may include in the final rule revisions to any provisions in part 585 that are a logical outgrowth of this proposed rule, consistent with the Administrative Procedure Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label comments with RIN/docket and organize them
rubrics_metrics.description: Label your comments on this proposed rule with RIN 1010-AE04 or docket number BOEM-2020-0033.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize your comments sequentially by the preamble section heading or by the proposed rule section number when addressing specific rule sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain positions and propose alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why you agree or disagree with specific provisions; suggest alternative provisions or provide substitute language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe your assumptions, information, and data used in formulating your comments. Provide specific examples to illustrate your concerns and suggested alternatives. Explain your views clearly and succinctly. Ensure your comments are submitted by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate SAP requirement for met buoys (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule would eliminate both the SAP requirement for met buoys and the limited lease requirement for installing off-lease met towers and met buoys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Off-lease met towers and met buoys would continue to require USACE permits under section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act. BOEM's SAP process is well suited for met towers but has proven unreasonably burdensome and redundant with USACE for met buoys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase survey flexibility (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defer certain geotechnical survey requirements (e.g., boreholes, vibracores, grab samplers, cone penetrometer tests and other penetrative methods) until after COP approval, but before construction, to allow more time and flexibility for project design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM's existing requirement for detailed geotechnical data for each turbine location in the COP is burdensome because turbine locations may be uncertain at COP submittal. BOEM's guidelines for geotechnical surveys are available online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand CVA role and change 'certify' to 'verify' (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand the certified verification agent (CVA)'s role to include verification of the design and commissioning of critical safety systems and change regulatory language from 'certify'/'certification' to 'verify'/'verification'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with industry standards, may encourage more firms to serve as CVAs, allow BOEM approval of CVA nominations before COP submittal, and permit separate FDRs and FIRs for major components and specialized CVAs to verify specific components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish a Public Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a Secretary commitment to publish a schedule of anticipated lease sales that BOEM intends to hold in the subsequent 5 years, updated at least once every 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The schedule would provide a general description of the area of each proposed lease sale, the anticipated quarter of each sale, and reasons for changes made to the previously issued leasing schedule, if any. Comments on timing and scope can be made during public comment opportunities during the planning process (e.g., Request for Interest, Call for Information and Nominations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform renewable energy auction regulations (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganize and clarify pre- and post-auction procedures, address use of bidding credits, deter potential bidder collusion, and more clearly outline auction processes and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify actions if a provisional winner fails to meet obligations or if an existing lease is relinquished, contracted, or cancelled. Preserve the option to use multiple factor auctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor financial assurance requirements and instruments (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor financial assurance requirements to align with actual risk by allowing incremental funding of decommissioning accounts per a BOEM-approved schedule during the lease term and expand acceptable categories of financial assurance instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM requires financial assurances to protect the U.S. taxpayer against potential liabilities from defaults. Acceptable instruments include surety bonds, Treasury securities, AAA-rated securities, insurance, self-insurance, third-party guaranties, and decommissioning accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify safety management system (SMS) requirements (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the information requirements for safety management systems and add two safety reporting requirements; incentivize lessees and grant holders to obtain SMS certification from an accredited conformity assessment body (CAB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtaining SMS certification from an accredited CAB could reduce the frequency and intensity of BOEM regulatory oversight activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restructure commercial lease terms and other technical changes (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restructure commercial lease terms into four periods tied to activities required to develop the lease; explicitly allow regulatory departures before and after a lease or grant is issued; authorize civil penalties without notice/time for corrective action when violations cause or threaten serious, irreparable, or immediate harm; add lease segregation/consolidation procedures; standardize annual rental rates per acre across most grants; and correct technical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions are part of numerous additional proposed changes that do not fit other categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority and competitive requirement for leases/grants
rubrics_metrics.description: OCS Lands Act subsection 8(p) authorizes the Secretary to award OCS leases, ROWs, and RUEs for renewable energy and generally requires competitive awards unless the Secretary determines competitive interest does not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary delegated leasing authority to BOEM; BOEM's renewable energy regulations are codified at 30 CFR part 585.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leases, ROWs, RUEs required prior to activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A lease, ROW, or RUE is required before a person may construct, operate, or maintain a renewable energy facility on the OCS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commercial lease authorizes activities for distribution, sale, or other commercial use; a limited lease authorizes supporting activities not producing energy for sale beyond a specified limit; leases may also be issued to Federal agencies or States for research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM discretion to issue regulatory departures
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may approve departures from its regulations if documented in writing, consistent with the OCS Lands Act, protect the environment/public health/safety/third party rights, and are necessary to facilitate activities, conserve resources, or protect life/property/environment/archaeological resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive leasing process steps and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM initiates leasing with a request for interest, typically followed by a Call for Information and Nominations; publishes a Proposed Sale Notice (PSN) and then a Final Sale Notice (FSN) at least 30 calendar days before the auction date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PSN invites public comment; BOEM may incorporate comments into the FSN. The FSN finalizes areas, auction procedures, and lease provisions and may provide a mock auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction types and multiple factor bidding
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing regulations specify four auction types and six bidding systems; BOEM may choose the auction format and bidding system in the FSN. Multiple factor bidding may allow non-monetary components (e.g., technical merit, financing and economics, compatibility with State and local needs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid acceptance, antitrust review, and bidder obligations timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After auction, BOEM implements a statutorily mandated 30-day antitrust review by DOJ and FTC. If no concerns and no appeals pending, BOEM typically accepts the winning bid within 90 calendar days. The winning bidder has 10 business days from receipt of unsigned copies to sign and return, provide financial assurance, and pay balance due; must pay first 12 months' rent within 45 calendar days of receiving unsigned copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may extend deadlines for good cause. BOEM reserves the right to withdraw an OCS area prior to lease execution and refund the bid deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid rejection and appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may reject any bid determined to be inadequate, illegal, the result of anti-competitive behavior, administrative error, or unusual bidding patterns. A bidder may appeal to the BOEM Director within 15 business days of bid rejection to seek reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM will send a response affirming or reversing the final bid decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: DNCI and noncompetitive lease issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM concludes that competitive interest is absent in a lease area, BOEM may publish a Determination of No Competitive Interest (DNCI) and may offer a noncompetitive lease to the sole interested developer after consultations and receipt of requisite certifications, information, and payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration remedies and assignment liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may enforce lease/grant terms and take remedies including corrective actions, cessation orders, civil penalties, and lease or grant termination. Lessees and grant holders may designate an operator; both are jointly and severally responsible for complying with regulations. Assignors remain jointly and severally liable for liabilities that accrued before BOEM approves an assignment; assignees must be legally, technically, and financially qualified under 30 CFR part 585.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease suspension, renewal, and termination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a lease or grant can be suspended by request approved by BOEM, by BOEM order, when necessary to comply with a judicial decree, to avoid imminent threat of irreparable harm, or for national security. A suspension pauses the running of the lease term and may suspend lease payments. BOEM may approve renewals based on enumerated criteria. Leases may terminate by expiration, cancellation for enumerated reasons (including fraud), partial cancellation (reducing area), or voluntary relinquishment subject to BOEM approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments and financial assurance mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessees and grant holders must make regular payments to the U.S. Treasury. Before bidding a competitive lease, submit a bid deposit. Obtaining a lease noncompetitively requires an acquisition fee. Lessees and grant holders must make annual rental payments based on acreage; ROW rentals are based on right-of-way length and acreage. Under a commercial lease, an operating fee replaces rental when commercial operations begin (calculated by regulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations provide mechanisms to request reduction or waiver. BOEM will distribute revenue under section 8(g) to eligible coastal States for projects within three miles seaward of a State's submerged lands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance amounts and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee must provide financial assurance in the amount of $100,000 before acquiring a commercial lease and supplemental financial assurance before approval of a SAP and a COP, and before commencement of construction. Financial assurance requirements for limited leases and grants have an initial requirement of $300,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM bases requirements on cumulative liabilities and decommissioning cost estimates. Acceptable instruments include surety bonds, Treasury securities, AAA-rated securities, insurance, self-insurance, third-party guaranties, and BOEM-approved decommissioning accounts. BOEM requires maintenance of financial assurance until no less than 7 years after a lease or grant ends and sets procedures for lapses, reductions in value, or surety termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP submittal content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee planning to install site assessment facilities must submit a Site Assessment Plan (SAP) that includes general structural, design, fabrication, and installation information for each type of facility associated with the proposed site assessment activities, plus environmental information gathered from geological and geophysical surveys, hazard surveys, baseline environmental surveys, and archaeological surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SAP must be submitted no later than 12 months after lease issuance. BOEM may approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications. BOEM will determine if proposed facilities are complex or significant; if not complex, activities may begin upon approval; if complex, additional requirements in subpart G apply. Implementation must follow a Safety Management System (SMS). SAP approval does not authorize building facilities for commercial energy production.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP submittal requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before fabricating and installing any facility for commercial operations, a lessee must submit a Construction and Operations Plan (COP) describing facilities for commercial operations, project easements, onshore/support facilities, all proposed activities (construction, commercial operations, decommissioning), general structural and project design, fabrication and installation information, and results of geological, geotechnical, biological, and archaeological surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The COP must be submitted at least 6 months before the five-year site assessment term expires. BOEM may approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP requirements for limited leases/grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities under a limited lease, ROW, or RUE must be approved by a General Activities Plan (GAP) submitted no later than 12 months after lease or grant issuance and describing facilities, project easements, onshore/support facilities, design, fabrication, construction, use, decommissioning, and survey results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may approve, disapprove, or approve with modifications and will determine if facilities are complex/significant (if so, subpart G applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart G: design, fabrication, and installation of complex/significant facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart G requires detailed design, fabrication, and installation information for each complex or significant facility to ensure safe operation using accepted engineering practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations require an independent assessment by certified verification agents (CVAs) experienced in offshore marine facility design/fabrication/installation. CVAs are hired by lessees but report directly to BOEM and must not create conflicts of interest. Subpart G outlines CVA circumstances, nomination and waiver processes, and CVA duties. If CVA is waived, the project engineer must perform the same duties (but not as an independent third-party reviewer).

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR and CVA verification/certification
rubrics_metrics.description: After BOEM approval of the SAP, COP, or GAP, a lessee or grant holder must submit a Facility Design Report (FDR) describing final design of all proposed facilities. The CVA must certify (or verify under proposed changes) that the facilities are designed to withstand environmental and functional load conditions appropriate for the intended service life at the proposed location.
